verdicts.quote: the selected member gets a confirmed booking without having to claim or accept the place
the member whose current entry was accepted first receives it
verdicts.missing: Tie-breaking is deliberately left unprescribed (C-27), and nothing says whether a membership tier or staff override can jump the queue.

verdicts.quote: A member with a booking from the waitlist can cancel under the same conditions as a member with an otherwise equivalent ordinary booking.
verdicts.missing: Whether a no-show or late cancellation on an automatically created booking counts against the member under the existing no-show policy.

verdicts.quote: If cancellation releases 1 place and a member is eligible on the waitlist, 1 waiting member gets a confirmed booking.
verdicts.missing: The trigger is stated, but not that promotion runs as background work or how promptly it must happen.

verdicts.quote: concurrent actions that could consume it produce at most 1 new confirmed booking for the place
Members try booking or joining at the same time, or a waiter leaves while a place opens. Each member sees the outcome of their action. A place is assigned at most once
verdicts.missing: Whether a member who books directly while their own entry is being promoted can end up with two bookings, and which action wins.

verdicts.quote: an eligible member's join cannot be refused solely because of the number of entries already on the waitlist
When the existing booking rules make it permanently too late to book an occurrence, members no longer see active entries for it.
An increase that creates bookable places allows the waitlist to advance. A reduction does not cancel existing bookings through waitlist processing.
A member checking an entry after the occurrence has been canceled or removed no longer sees the entry as active.
the original entry continues to count from its original acceptance
verdicts.missing: Join time and active or ended states are implied, but the spec doesn't say whether queue position is stored or derived, or list the record's fields.

verdicts.quote: When the existing booking rules make it permanently too late to book an occurrence, members no longer see active entries for it.
verdicts.missing: What happens to the ended entries after the class runs and how long they are kept.

verdicts.quote: A regular member checking their own waitlist status is not shown the identities of other waiters.
verdicts.missing: Whether the member sees their own position in the queue; C-4 only says they can tell they are still waiting.

verdicts.quote: lets members join eligible full occurrences without an operator configuring the waitlist ... the requested behavior applies wherever existing class capacity makes an occurrence full
A member can use the same booking actions as before for an occurrence with a place available to them through ordinary booking.
An otherwise eligible member can join a still-full occurrence created before the update.
